messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Runtime latency spike detected for /v1/generate across us-west-2 canary cluster. P90 increased from 120ms -> 1.8s at 12:04 UTC. Autotrigger: deploy 2026-02-12T11:58Z. Paging on-call. https://ops.redwood/incident/IR-2026-209

alice (oncall): I'm on it. Noting recent deploy at 11:58. Starting the incident runbook now.

bob (eng-sre): Seeing kernel fallback churn on the canary nodes: frequent kernel selection swaps and prefetch evictions. Logs: `kernel_select: fallback->tier2` repeated. CPU 95% on the batcher process.

carol (eng-runtime): Confirmed. Canary traces show a sudden increase in microbatch sizes and reordering that spikes KV cache misses. Suggest immediate mitigation: disable aggressive batching feature flag `batching.v2.aggressive` or roll back canary.

alice (oncall): Trying flip: `kubectl patch cm ff-config -p '{"data":{"batching.v2.aggressive":"false"}}'`

deploy-bot: :gear: Feature flag flip requested by alice. Applying to canary pool (us-west-2-canary).

bob (eng-sre): Observing partial improvement in latency within 45s, but throughput is unstable. Some pods still evict heavy KV sets; kernel fallback events persist on a subset of hosts.

dave (support): I'm seeing 3 customer tickets for timeouts in us-west-2; surface level: increased 5xx rate ~0.6% (baseline 0.02%). Not yet customer-impacting at scale but noisy.

eve (cs): Notifying affected customers (P1 list) with a short statement: "We are investigating elevated latency in US-West canary; full service not impacted for most users."

carol (eng-runtime): We should prepare rollback plan. If flipping flag doesn't fully stabilize within 10m, we do a full canary rollback. Running `deployctl rollback --canary --to=2026-02-12T11:45Z` as standby.

alice (oncall): Agree. Waiting on stability window. If we rollback, coordinate evictions to avoid warmup surge.

bob (eng-sre): Noted risk: rollback will cause transient cache cold starts; recommend staged drain of canary hosts: `for host in canary_hosts: cordon && drain --grace=60` then resume with old image.

deploy-bot: :warning: Rollback initiated by carol at 12:18 UTC. Target revision: 2026-02-12T11:45Z.

alice (oncall): Rollback in progress. Monitoring p95/p99 and customer 5xx.

bob (eng-sre): Early signs good — p90 down to 210ms, p95 trending toward baseline. Kernel fallback events dropping sharply. Disk I/O on batcher lower.

frank (eng-mgr): Heads-up: we'll keep dedicated monitoring for the next 2 hours. Need postmortem addition: why `batching.v2.aggressive` combo with a model-specific kv pattern caused fallback.

dave (support): Updating ticket queue: notifying customers that rollback completed and we're continuing investigation.

alice (oncall): Preparing handoff to daytime on-call at 14:00 UTC. Handoff summary: recent deploy 11:58 triggered canary instability -> kernel fallback & KV churn -> attempted FF flip reduced impact but not stable -> rollback at 12:18 restored latency. Ongoing: root cause analysis, telemetry capture, and postmortem.

eve (cs): I'll follow up with the 3 customers this afternoon with an incident update.

carol (eng-runtime): Action items for follow-up: 1) capture canary heap/proc samples from failed hosts, 2) replay traffic against staging with `batching.v2.aggressive=false/true` toggles, 3) add a safeguard to block `batching.v2.aggressive` for canaries when model_kv_miss_rate > 0.05.

bob (eng-sre): Adding a short-term alert: if kernel_fallback_rate > 0.01 for any cluster, auto-cut canary traffic.

alice (oncall): Last check: p99 still slightly elevated (2.4s) on a very small slice — watching. If no regressions, I'll mark incident as mitigated at handoff.

frank (eng-mgr): Thanks team. Please annotate all commands and timelines in the incident doc. We'll triage postmortem priority and owners after handoff. :thumbsup:

alice (oncall): Handoff at 14:00UTC to @carol (day oncall). Leaving incident as "Mitigated - monitoring".
